why: Five Gigs and one ready 8-power Unit. Attacking now steals one Gig, which is the biggest immediate gain on the board and is what a one-ply agent takes; it ends the turn on six. Equipping the +2 Gear first is worth almost nothing on the board, but it lifts the attacker to 10 power, and steal_count(10) is two Gigs, which is the game. The plan's A-then-C in its smallest honest form — and the whole of it inside one turn, which is why the horizon is 1. Built like a real mid-game board — three Legends and a real remaining deck a side — so a value head reading list size, undrawn fraction and Legend RAM is not extrapolating on it.
retired: Dropped from data/arena/delayed.json when ruling 027 landed: random play now wins it 6 of 16 trials, over the suite’s 25% floor, because a Legend that may pay for its own Call gives random another way through. It is still exactly what this test needs — a setup move that must precede a payoff — so it lives here now. An ISMCTS behaviour test should not depend on a position clearing a different suite’s statistical bar; that coupling is what broke, and moving the file fixes it.
